target_customer: Food distributors and wholesalers (who pay for the platform) and the convenience store owners who order from them
problem: Convenience store owners buy from 10 to 15 suppliers a week through phone calls, paper invoices and warehouse trips; distributors lack online ordering, invoicing and payment collection.
business_model: B2B SaaS and marketplace for distributors: branded ordering portal, invoicing and payments
product_category: Wholesale ordering software for convenience retail

founders.name: Aamir Hudda
education: Computer Science and Business, UC Berkeley
founders.background_notes: Product roles at Meta and eBay per YC page.

founders.name: Joseph Yeh
education: Computer Science and Math, UC Berkeley
previous_startups: Three YC companies (not named on the YC page)

technical_complexity.rationale: Ordering app and distributor portal are standard CRUD and integrations; the hard part is distributor data and ERP integration.

defensibility.rationale: Once a distributor moves ordering and invoicing to the platform there is some lock in, but the product is copyable.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: McLane introduced its own online marketplace for retailers in March 2024 per the convenience.org trade site, an incumbent building a similar wedge.

market_need_then: YC description says store owners spend hours ordering across 10 to 15 suppliers and lose revenue to stockouts; the company page says convenience stores buy from distributors by paper invoice and phone. No independent dated demand data found.

identity.voice_and_tone: Direct productivity promises such as say goodbye to paper invoices and phone orders

brand_strength.rationale: No press or community about the brand found; a common English word with several unrelated companies sharing the name.

pivots.from: Single app for stores to buy across all suppliers (marketplace)
pivots.to: White label ordering, invoicing and payments portal sold to food distributors
pivots.why: Not stated; inferred from comparing the YC description with the current company page, so date unknown

outcome_analysis: Attain started as a marketplace letting convenience stores order from many suppliers and now sells distributors a branded ordering, invoicing and payments portal, with an iOS app in the store. Only a pre-seed record tied to YC and Soma Capital is public and nothing indicates shutdown or exit. With so little public information the company's trajectory cannot be judged.
notes: Competitors list left empty: searches (Lula, Digiday 2018 article, trade press) found no dated wholesale ordering rivals near March 2022; Lula is a consumer and online ordering vendor, not a rival wedge. The pivot is inferred from two descriptions and flagged as such. Pre-seed listing at VCBacked (Mar 2022, undisclosed amount, Y Combinator and Soma Capital) is a single aggregator and not recorded as a round. MClane source is dated 2024, after founding.
